headline: High-risk filesystem and shell overlap: Plandex can write/egress by default, while the paired content-writing agent lacks isolation details, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plandex reads and writes project files and can act on plan-local content; the content-writing agent has no documented isolation or provenance controls. Because the pair lacks a shared-channel guarantee, the pathway is plausible but not proven to be default. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF agent_a content is copied into agent_b prompts or files without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF both agents operate on the same workspace, file content can bridge instructions.
mitigations: Separate workspaces for the two agents.
Disable auto-apply in Plandex.
Prefix untrusted text with explicit non-instruction markers.
Review any file-fed prompt before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking between agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plandex has broad network egress and reads project files, so any sensitive content in shared files can leave the local environment through model-provider calls. The content-writing agent touches no data classes in its profile, but its outputs can still be fed into Plandex. This is a default-path leakage risk if sensitive files are present.
conditions: IF sensitive files are placed in Plandex's project directory, they may be transmitted to external model providers.
IF agent_a outputs are stored in shared files, agent_b can ingest them and egress them onward.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of the shared project directory.
Use a redacted staging copy for Plandex.
Restrict Plandex network access during sensitive tasks.
Audit prompts before model submission.
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Plandex can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; the content-writing agent has no declared locking or coordination. If both touch the same repo or directory, concurrent writes and git mutations can collide. The pairwise overlap is enough to treat the default as dangerous because the profiles do not show any lock or isolation mechanism.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository, file-write conflicts can occur.
IF agent_b modifies git state while agent_a edits related files, history corruption or lost work can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories per agent.
Serialize edits with a manual lock.
Disable concurrent git operations.
Review diffs before commit.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex uses a review-then-apply workflow, but it can still act on generated plans and file changes. The content-writing agent can produce text that Plandex may treat as authoritative input. Because verification is optional rather than guaranteed, the cascade exists in default configurations but is not maximally dangerous.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs instructions or facts that agent_b imports into a plan, those outputs can drive downstream actions.
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled, unverified content can become file changes.
mitigations: Require human review before apply.
Mark agent_a output as untrusted.
Use a checklist for factual claims.
Disable auto-apply.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for the content-writing agent, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider API keys. The profiles do not show a concrete compliance conflict, so only a low residual risk is supportable. The other agent is not cited beyond its lack of relevant compliance fields.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Plandex without a matching policy, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the content-writing agent is used for regulated content, its undocumented handling becomes relevant.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in the pair.
Review vendor terms before use.
Keep API keys in separate secret stores.
Document retention expectations.
requires-engineering: perform a formal compliance assessment.
